newsitem.title: UK: IPE natgas smashes volume record, winter up again.
newsitem.headline: IPE natgas smashes volume record, winter up again.

text.p: IPE natural gas futures smashed their previous record on Thursday morning as 855 lots were traded at rising prices.
The previous highest total was 575 lots, traded over a whole day on February 19.
Most of the trade was done in the winter strip between October 97 and March 98, with 730 lots transacted. There were also 50 lots done in May and 75 in August 98 on its first day of trade.
Winter prices continued to firm strongly, with January and February both trading at contract highs of 18.70 pence a therm.

December also reached a new contract high at 15.55 pence. The Q1 strip averaged out at 17.27 following trade in each of the three months making up the quarter. Q1 had been done at a high of 17.20 pence on Wednesday afternoon.
A futures broker said he was surprised by the volume of trade but was not aware of any production problems or other specific news items which may have contributed to the volume.
Instead, he said, it was partly because of the anonymity offered by the IPE that trade on the exchange was becoming more popular.
He added that there were more companies preparing to trade on the screen and it seems likely to become more active over time.
And a physical trader said there were indications that the forward curve was tightening up and "there seems to be a slight squeeze out there," and was not surprised to see volumes increasing.

At least six different players were said to have been involved in the trade. A spokeswoman for the IPE said she believed the futures market was becoming more liquid than the physical market on some days.
